newsitem.title: FRANCE: France urges nationals to leave eastern Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France urges nationals to leave eastern Zaire.

text.p: France urged its few nationals remaining in eastern Zaire to leave on Saturday and urged the European Community to boost relief to civilians caught in fighting between Tutsi rebels against Zairean troops.

A Foreign Ministry statement said ministry officials held an emergency meeting to look into humanitarian needs and called for the emergency United Nations mission proposed by U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali to urgently visit the region.

France's Junior Minister for Emergency Humanitarian Action Xavier Emmanuelli contacted the European Commission to discuss extra relief for civilians, and the issue would be raised at a European Union Foreign Ministers meeting on Monday, it said.
A ministry spokesman said most of the about 100 French nationals in Kivu had already left and those who remained were missionaries and aid workers.
The U.N. pulled its aid workers out of eastern Zaire on Saturday as conflict threatened to engulf much of the region.
The rebels were reported to have captured two towns in the east of the country, panicking refugees. Nearly half-a-million refugees are now estimated to be on the move.
A string of camps in Zaire houses 1.1. million Rwandan refugees, including perpetrators of the 1994 genocide in Rwanda in which Hutus killed up to one million Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko has been absent from the country for more than two months, receiving cancer treatment in Switzerland, and his long illness is fuelling the crisis.
